newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil set to raise EU's car import quotas - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil set to raise EU's car import quotas - paper.

text.p: Brazil plans to raise significantly its car import quotas for the European Union as of August 21 in a move to avoid a car dispute in the World Trade Organization (WTO), Gazeta Mercantil newspaper reported.
Gazeta said the European Union's quota could be raised to 14,000 cars a year from 9,700.

The car quota system was settled last year with Japan, South Korea and nations from the European Union as a concession to those countries after Brazilintroduced higher import tariffs for carmakers without a manufacturing base in the country.
Under the quota system, carmakers from the EU, Japan and South Korea were allowed to export a total of 50,000 vehicles a year to Brazil at a 35 percent tariff rate.

An increase in the car quotas would be the Brazilian response to growing pressure from the European Union. Newspapers have reported that the EU appears set to ask the WTO to create a panel to look into Brazil's automotive regime.
